title: Clinical split-mouth study: Comparison of the Clean-and-Seal concept (Perisolv® & Hyadent BG®) in combination with anti-infective therapy (AIT) versus anti-infective therapy (AIT) alone on the modification of clinical parameters in patients with periodontitis.
summary: Gum inflammation can lead to gum recession and loss of support for the teeth. There are different treatments to clean the gums, reduce inflammation, and improve the stability of the teeth. This study aims to investigate which of two treatments is more effective: anti-infective therapy alone or the combination of anti-infective therapy with the “Clean and Seal” method (using Perisolv® and Hyadent BG®). Each patient will receive both treatments in different parts of the mouth. The study will examine how well the gums attach to the teeth, the depth of the gum pockets, whether the gums recede, whether they bleed during examination, and the overall improvement of gum health. The evaluations will take place at three, six, and twelve months.

interventions.name:
Intervention Group 1 (Test group – Split-mouth)

Each study participant will receive both the test and control treatments: in one jaw, periodontal therapy will be performed as a combination of AIT and the Kink-and-Target concept (test group), while in the contralateral jaw, AIT alone will be appli

Intervention Group 2 (Control group – Split-mouth)

In the contralateral jaw, patients receive non-surgical anti-infective periodontal therapy (AIT) alone, consisting of mechanical subgingival instrumentation without adjunctive chemical biofilm disruption or sealing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
•	Untreated patients with severe/advanced periodontitis (Stage III/IV) with slow/moderate progression (Grade A/B)
•	Only individuals capable of giving consent, aged ≥ 18 years
•	Presence of at least one probing depth (PD) ≥ 6 mm per jaw
•	Single-rooted teeth or multi-rooted teeth without furcation involvement
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion Criteria:
•	Patients with systemic diseases, particularly:
o	Use of bisphosphonates
o	Ongoing or previous chemotherapy
o	Ongoing or previous radiotherapy
o	Infectious diseases such as HIV or Hepatitis A, B, or C
•	Pregnant or breastfeeding women
•	Smokers of more than 10 cigarettes per day
•	Periodontal treatment within the last 2 years
•	Long-term antibiotic or anti-inflammatory therapy within 6 months prior to periodontal treatment
•	Furcation involvement
•	Acute periodontal or endodontic abscesses
•	Wisdom teeth (third molars) are not included in the treatment
